File a Mechanics Lien in Walton County, FL

Recording a mechanics lien in Walton County, Florida means going to the Clerk of the Circuit Court — the clerk of the circuit court (official records). First-page recording runs approximately $10–$15. The state deadline for filing is 90 days.

What you need to file in Walton County

To record a valid mechanics lien in Walton County, you need:

  • A completed Claim of Lien or Lien Affidavit — most states provide a statutory form; Texas requires notarization and specific homestead language. Verify the form requirements for Florida before filing.
  • The correct legal property description — not just a street address. A wrong legal description can void the lien. Pull it from the property deed or the county assessor's parcel map.
  • Proof of preliminary notice (if required) — some states require you to file evidence that you sent the required preliminary notice. Attach the certified-mail return receipt if Florida requires it.
  • The recording fee — approximately $10–$15 for the first page in Walton County, plus additional per-page charges.

Florida lien deadlines for Walton County

The mechanics lien filing deadline for Florida is 90 days. This deadline applies regardless of which Florida county you record in — it's set by state statute, specifically Fla. Stat. ch. 713 The preliminary notice deadline is 45 days from first furnishing.

After recording — what's next?

Once the lien is recorded in Walton County, you must serve a copy on the property owner (if Florida requires it — some states mandate service within 5 days of recording). Keep the certified-mail return receipt. Then enforce (foreclose) the lien within your state's enforcement window — typically 1–2 years from the recording date.
